consensus_summary: Consensus centers on Issachar symbolizing discernment or 'understanding of the times' (1 Chr 12:32), the dominant modern reading, with strong secondary traditions of burden-bearing labor/servitude (Gen 49:14-15), wages/reward from the name etymology (Gen 30:18), and contentment/prosperity in tents (Deut 33:18-19). One response (D) inverts the ranking, making the donkey/burden emblem primary and the times-discernment reading a common alternative. All agree these motifs form a recognizable cluster without a fully settled single meaning.
book_summary: The book presents Issachar as a composite figure — 'the hireling who owns the field': strong donkey-bearer, humble bower, tent-dweller, discerner of appointed times, provider of royal provision (1 Kgs 4), and willing warrior in the valley (Judg 5:15). It then adds a celestial identification: Issachar in the heavenly camp is Virgo in the east ('the place of beginnings and returns'), identified with sapphire and the full moon.
consensus_core_identification: Issachar = discernment of the times (dominant), alongside burden-bearing labor, wages/reward, and settled contentment as recognized alternatives.
book_core_identification: Issachar = a unified composite of hireling/wages, donkey burden-bearer, tent-dweller, discerner of times, provisioner, and valley-warrior — mapped cosmically onto Virgo, sapphire, and the full moon in the eastern camp.
boundary_disagreement: The book does not reject any consensus meaning; instead it fuses the discernment, burden-bearing, wages, and contentment motifs (each treated by consensus as competing alternatives) into a single integrated identification, and extends the symbol into territory no consensus response mentions: royal provisioning (1 Kgs 4:7,17; 1 Chr 12:40), military willingness (Judg 5:15, noted only as 'rare' by Response C), camp position in the east (Num 2:3-5), and the astronomical/gemological assignments (Virgo, sapphire, full moon).
material_contradiction: None. Nothing in the book's entry requires rejecting the consensus identifications; the celestial layer is additive rather than substitutive.
rationale: Reduced to its minimum core, the book's identification incorporates every major consensus motif — hire/wages, strong donkey, tents, understanding the times — so the central referent is preserved, ruling out DIVERGENT. But it is not a mere MATCH: the book materially changes the shape of the symbol by (a) unifying the alternatives into one composite portrait rather than ranking one meaning as primary, and (b) extending the symbol's coverage with cases absent from all consensus responses, most notably the Virgo/sapphire/full-moon cosmological identification. This is a real change in extension and precision at the boundary while keeping the consensus category intact, which is the definition of REFINED. NOVEL is not warranted because the recognizable consensus motifs plainly cover the bulk of the book's core.
strongest_objection: One could argue for NOVEL on the grounds that the book's distinctive core is the heavenly-camp identification (Virgo, sapphire, full moon), which no consensus response or alternative remotely anticipates and which the printed scriptures do not support (Num 2:3-5 gives only camp position, not a zodiac sign or gem). If the celestial mapping is treated as the true center of the book's identification rather than an added layer, the composite biblical portrait would be mere scaffolding and the classification should shift toward NOVEL.
